title: Linux & the Command Line
summary: The floor everything else stands on. Filesystem layout, permissions, processes, redirection and pipes until the shell stops feeling foreign.

title: Networking Essentials
summary: How packets actually move. The OSI model in practice, TCP/IP, DNS and HTTP read straight off the wire.

title: Scripting & Automation
summary: Stop doing things twice. Python and Bash for parsing, fuzzing, and gluing tools into a workflow you own.

title: Cryptography & Ciphers
summary: Classical ciphers through modern primitives — and, more usefully, the ways real systems misuse them.

title: Web Security — OWASP Top 10
summary: The category that wins most CTFs and pays most bounties. Injection, broken access control, XSS, SSRF — demonstrated in a lab you can break.

title: Network & Wireless Attacks
summary: Enumeration, service exploitation, pivoting, and how wireless authentication falls apart under pressure.

title: Reverse Engineering
summary: Source to assembly and back. Read a stripped binary, find the check, and understand why it was there.

title: Binary Exploitation
summary: Memory corruption from first principles — stack layout, overflows, ROP, and the mitigations built to stop them.

title: Digital Forensics
summary: Where the defensive half begins. Disk and memory artefacts, timeline reconstruction, and evidence handling that survives scrutiny.

title: Malware Analysis
summary: Safe detonation in an isolated lab. Behavioural triage, indicators of compromise, and writing up what a sample actually does.

title: Blue Team & Detection
summary: The SOC side of the house. Log pipelines, detection engineering, and triaging an alert queue without drowning in it.

title: Cloud Security & Bug Bounty
summary: Where the ladder points outward. Cloud identity and misconfiguration, then scope, safe harbour, and writing a report a programme will pay for.
